issue_context.title: IPv6 Compliance RFC4861: Router Advertisement Processing, Cur Hop Limit [v6LC.2.2.13 Part B]
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

250

### Used distribution

Embedded Linux - Debian-based

### Linux kernel version used

5.15.71-rt51+gc36e774d0d9a

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

aarch64

### Component

systemd-networkd

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

**Purpose**: Verify that a node properly processes the Cur Hop Limit field of a Router Advertisement.

#### Reference
[RFC4861](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4861.txt) Neighbor Discovery – Sections 4.2 and 6.3.4

From section 4.2. Router Advertisement Message Format:
```
Cur Hop Limit        8-bit unsigned integer.  The default value that
                     should be placed in the Hop Count field of the IP
                     header for outgoing IP packets.  A value of zero
                     means unspecified (by this router).
```

From section 6.3.4. Processing Received Router Advertisements:
```
If the received Cur Hop Limit value is non-zero, the host SHOULD set
its CurHopLimit variable to the received value.
```



### Unexpected behaviour you saw

networkd ignores the RA's CurHopLimit parameter.

For comparison, stopping `networkd` and configuring the interface via `/etc/network/interfaces` results in a successful protocol exchange.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

The attached zip file has a `legacy` folder, where the network was configured via `/etc/network/interfaces` and a `networkd` folder, where the network was managed by `networkd`. The PCAP in the `legacy` folder demonstrates the expected protocol exchange, whereas the PCAP in the `networkd` folder demonstrates the failure.

Specifically, in the file `v6LC_2_2_13b-Net0-20230707042202-filtered.pcapng`, packet 11 shows the RA setting `Cur hop limit: 100`. The ping reply in packet 13 shows networkd has not used the `Cur hop limit` from the RA and instead uses the value 64.

[2_2_13b - Router Advertisement Processing, Cur Hop Limit.zip](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/files/12075238/2_2_13b.-.Router.Advertisement.Processing.Cur.Hop.Limit.zip)


### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

Reference: [IPv6 Core Conformance Specification](https://www.ipv6ready.org/docs/Core_Conformance.pdf), Test v6LC.2.2.13, part B.

@yuwata, it's a very simple protocol exchange...

This is the summary of the exchange and why it fails... Consider three nodes with a private IPv6 network between them.  The nodes are: TR1 (Test Router 1), TN1 (test node 1) and NUT (Node Under Test).

```
     TR1 ----+
             |
             +---- NUT
             |
     TN1 ----+
```

I've attached the PCAP and debug log in the zip file.  Below, the values in square brackets match the packets in the PCAP.

1. TN1 sends ping request and observes the NUT's ping reply with `HopLimit=64` (the default) [Pkt 7 & 10]
2. TR1 sends RA with `CurHopLimit=100` [Pkt 11]
3. TN1 sends ping request and observes the NUT's ping reply with `HopLimit=64` FAIL! Should be 100. [Pkt 12 & 13]

The test fails, because the ping reply in step 3, ought to have a `HopLimit=100`.

[v6LC_2_2_13b.zip](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/files/14161745/v6LC_2_2_13b.zip)
